2. During the pendency of the petition, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amicably amongst themselves and have filed a joint affidavit of compromise before this Court.

The settlement insofar as the present petition is concerned reads as follows:
"JOINT AFFIDAVIT .... .... ....
3. After detailed negotiation and intervention of elder and well wishers from both the parties, the Petitioner No.1 and Respondent No.2 have resolved the dispute amicably.
4. In view of the settlement, the Respondent No.1 has by withdrawing the allegations in the Complaint consented for quashing of the proceedings in C.C.No.26252/2019 pending on the file of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bangalore.
5.

In view of the settlement, the Petitioner No.1 & Respondent No.2 respectfully pray that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to quash the in C.C.No.26252/2019 pending on the file NC:
2023:KHC:20653 of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bangalore, in the interest of justice and equity."
3.

Since the offences alleged against the petitioners is punishable under Section 498A, 323 and 504 r/w 34 of the IPC of the IPC, which are not against the State or Society, and also in view of the compromise arrived at between the parties as aforesaid, I deem it appropriate to obliterate the proceedings pending against the petitioners.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Petition is disposed.
(ii) Impugned proceedings in C.C.No.26252/2019 pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru stands quashed qua the petitioners.
